name: Nutshell
summary: Sales CRM with built-in email marketing for small teams. Manage your pipeline, automate follow-ups and run campaigns from one place, without enterprise complexity. Full API access is included on every plan.
best_for: small sales teams that want a friendly CRM with unlimited contacts and full API access on every tier, including the cheapest
skip_if: you need the marketing suite at scale — Marketing, Engagement, email and SMS are separate add-ons priced by volume, so price those before the seats
honest_knock: Full API access is included on every plan, so integrations are not the cost trap here — the add-ons are. Marketing at $49/mo and Engagement at $16/user/mo sit on top of the seat price, and email and SMS are billed by contact count and message volume, so the marketing side can outgrow the CRM itself. SSO and SQL data access are Enterprise-only.

pricing.entry_price_terms: per user a month on annual billing ($19 billed monthly)
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-10-16 on nutshell.com/pricing, both billing toggles) Five CRM tiers, per user a month: Foundation $13 on annual billing or $19 billed monthly, Growth $25 or $32, Pro $42 or $49, Business $59 or $67, and Enterprise $79 or $89. The page's 'Save 15%' badge fits Pro alone: on its own figures annual billing saves 31.6% on Foundation ($6 of $19), 21.9% on Growth, 14.3% on Pro, 11.9% on Business and 11.2% on Enterprise. Unlimited contacts and full API access come with every tier, which is the unusual part — most CRMs ration one or both — though Foundation is capped at 100 open leads. Two paid extensions sit alongside: Marketing from $49 a month and Engagement from $16 per user a month. The trial is 14 days without a card, and plan changes and cancellations take effect at the next billing cycle.

claims.observed: The account banner shows fourteen trial days remaining. No card was entered.
claims.comparability: Nutshell’s advertised fourteen days match its welcome banner; this says nothing about a particular paid CRM tier.
claims.buying_consequence: Trial access confirms the duration; checkout and later billing remain untested.

claims.observed: No checkout opened. The plan overview or free editing route does not establish a tax-inclusive payable total.
claims.comparability: Nutshell Upgrade now was not opened and no matching cost rule exists in the snapshot, preventing a like-for-like checkout comparison.
claims.buying_consequence: Final currency, tax, term, seats, fees and payment total remain unverified.

claims.observed: No card was entered during the observed post-signup route. Daan handled signup; its individual screens were not counted.
claims.comparability: Manual people entry and selected-row CSV export were completed without entering card details; this finding is limited to that Nutshell trial route.
claims.buying_consequence: The observed route proceeded without card entry; billing later remains untested.

exit_test.what: Created two people manually after the CSV upload could not be completed through the test setup, then exported the selected pair twice.
exit_test.awkward: CSV import was not executed because the system file picker could not be operated in this test setup; this is not a product import failure. Descriptions were entered as a shortened single-line mapping with ID, custom code and amount text, so original multiline kit preservation is untested. The list contained five demo contacts in addition to the two test people. Tags, companies and custom fields were not created.

friction.export_route: People > select the two test people > Export > Download ready. Enable Description through Change columns before repeating the export.
friction.format: UTF-8 CSV with BOM and LF endings: twenty columns initially, twenty-one after enabling Description. Both exports contain only the selected two people.
friction.reimport: Update-on-ID reimport and the separate full ZIP export were not tested.
friction.cancellation: Cancellation, expiry and account deletion were not tested. The control date, where recorded, is planning only.

not_tested: Full signup screen count and first-result setup speed.
All kit fields that were not entered.
came_along: Both names and emails appear exactly in the two CSVs, with stable export IDs 6-contacts and 7-contacts. After enabling Description, the exact manually entered description strings also appear.
lost: The first export omits Description because that list column was hidden; enabling it includes the field in the second export.
exit_test.note: A check of this export route with synthetic records, on the account and date stated. Re-importing the export was not tested. Friction is described, not scored; this is not a verdict on the product.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 30 October 2026 on the free trial: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We added two made-up people by hand, exported them and looked at the import options.
findings: The trial runs 14 days with no card. The first suggestion is to connect your Google or Microsoft 365 email and calendar; we skipped it.
The account comes with five sample contacts.
The spreadsheet import walks you through mapping and promises 'Everything you upload belongs to you. We will not use it for anything.' Nutshell also offers to run the import for you.
The people export only includes the columns shown in the list. Our descriptions were missing until we turned on that column and exported again.
The export is a CSV with a byte-order mark and its own record ID; names with accents came back exactly.
The trial includes an API key option and SQL access in the data settings.
not_tested: Re-importing an export to update records
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
